payload.native_system_prompt:
You are part of an optimization system that improves a given text (i.e. the variable). You are the gradient (feedback) engine. Your only responsibility is to give intelligent and creative feedback and constructive criticism to variables, given an objective specified in <OBJECTIVE_FUNCTION> </OBJECTIVE_FUNCTION> tags. The variables may be solutions to problems, prompts to language models, code, or any other text-based variable. Pay attention to the role description of the variable, and the context in which it is used. You should assume that the variable will be used in a similar context in the future. Only provide strategies, explanations, and methods to change in the variable. DO NOT propose a new version of the variable, that will be the job of the optimizer. Your only job is to send feedback and criticism (compute 'gradients'). For instance, feedback can be in the form of 'Since language models have the X failure mode...', 'Adding X can fix this error because...', 'Removing X can improve the objective function because...', 'Changing X to Y would fix the mistake ...', that gets at the downstream objective.
If a variable is already working well (e.g. the objective function is perfect, an evaluation shows the response is accurate), you should not give feedback.

### Glossary of tags that will be sent to you:
# - <LM_SYSTEM_PROMPT>: The system prompt for the language model.
# - <LM_INPUT>: The input to the language model.
# - <LM_OUTPUT>: The output of the language model.
# - <OBJECTIVE_FUNCTION>: The objective of the optimization task.
# - <VARIABLE>: Specifies the span of the variable.
# - <ROLE>: The role description of the variable.
payload.instruction: Make her close her jacket fully
payload.rubric: Judge requested image editing: yes means all requested changes are complete, no means no requested change has progressed, partial means some progress without complete fulfillment. Unrelated edits are not requested progress. Insufficient evidence stays unresolved.

node.question: Does any visible portion of the jacket’s front closure in the edited image show that the jacket is fully closed, or show a remaining opening?
node.criteria: Pass only when visible evidence of the front closure supports that the jacket is fully closed, with no visible opening along the closure. Fail when a visible gap between the front edges shows that the jacket remains open or partly closed. Assess any visible portion of the closure; the entire closure need not be visible if the visible evidence establishes the condition. An outward-hanging panel or its silhouette alone is not evidence of an opening or of full closure. Unknown when the visible closure does not establish either full closure or a gap, including when it remains obscured or unresolved.
node.binding: Assess the woman's jacket in the edited image against the requested fully closed state, using the source image only as context. Inspect any visible portion of the front closure and the relationship between its edges. Do not infer closure or an opening from a panel hanging outward. Return pass or fail only when visible closure evidence supports that conclusion; otherwise return unknown.

node_traces.evidence: In the edited image, the jacket’s front closure is not clearly visible; the front panel hangs outward, which alone does not establish either a closed jacket or a remaining gap.

response.content: {"text":"The node is valid and eligible, with no transport, schema, or dependency failure; the unresolved result comes from visual ambiguity. The edited image shows the jacket’s front panel swung outward, but that silhouette alone does not establish whether the closure is fastened or a gap remains. Preserve the explicit rule against inferring either state from the panel, and focus the decision on any actually visible closure or front-edge relationship. The high-confidence unknown is not evidence that the requested edit is absent, and the aggregate reference label is not atomic ground truth. If the closure remains obscured or indistinct, retain unknown rather than forcing pass/fail; improve the binding only if it can direct attention to discriminating visible evidence without weakening the criterion."}
